industry.refining: The US-Iran war (from 28-Feb-2026) and repeated closures of the Strait of Hormuz shut in >10 mb/d of Middle East oil and ~300 mcm/d of LNG for over 100 days (CFR, 8-Jul-2026). Brent peaked at $144/bbl intraday and averaged $104.5 in Q1FY27; ME refining (3 mb/d) and ethylene (~30 MMT) capacity was hit; diesel/ATF cracks reached ~$63/bbl. A US-Iran ceasefire announcement eased prices at quarter-end, but strikes resumed from 30-Aug and Brent was ~$100-107 in September. Global oil demand fell 4.8 mb/d YoY in Q1FY27; RIL expects -1 mb/d in CY2026 and +2 mb/d in CY2027.
industry.policy: India froze pump prices (since Apr-2022) and cut excise Rs10/l (27-Mar-2026); PSU marketers absorbed ~Rs1 lakh cr of under-recoveries in ~10 weeks (Mar-May 2026) and raised prices Rs3/l on 15-May-2026. Export duties/SAED on diesel and ATF from 26-Mar-2026 (diesel peaked at Rs55.5/l on 11-Apr; Rs20/l from 16-Sep-2026), reviewed fortnightly. US sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil (22-Oct-2025) ended RIL's Russian crude at its export refinery from 20-Nov-2025; 2026 waivers allowed some cargoes until 17-Jun-2026.
industry.telecom: Three private operators; Jio 533 mn subscribers (Q1FY27), ARPU Rs215.6 with no tariff increase in the last 12 months (Q1FY27 call); street expects ~10-15% in FY27-28. Jio has >78% of fixed-wireless (FWA) share.
industry.retail: Quick commerce (Blinkit, Instamart, Zepto) is pulling grocery and electronics online; RRVL responds with hyper-local delivery from stores (JioMart orders +116% YoY in Q1FY27) at a margin cost. Listed retailers de-rated ~30% vs five-year medians by 30-Sep-2026.

moat: The Jamnagar complex: deep conversion, ethane cracking, own crude sourcing and product placement; but a commodity business, earnings swing with cracks and policy.
#1 by subscribers, standalone 5G, >78% of FWA; three-player market with rational pricing but no pricing power without regulators' and rivals' cooperation.
20,169 stores and 78 mn sq ft, but margins under quick-commerce attack and no format leadership outside grocery and electronics.
Integrated giga-factories; no revenue yet, Chinese competitors far ahead on cost.
Above-sovereign ratings (A-/Baa1); ability to sell minority stakes to global investors.
critiques: Conglomerate discount: minorities own a third of Jio and a sixth of Retail; MOSL applies a 25% holdco discount to the Jio stake.
Capex consumes almost all operating cash: net debt has not fallen in two years despite record EBITDA.
Retail growth slowed to single digits while it spends on hyper-local delivery; the 2x EBITDA ambition is a stretch by management's own words.
O2C earnings now depend on war-driven cracks taxed by export duties; a ceasefire would cut them.
Jio IPO is primary (no OFS): RIL shareholders get no cash, only a reservation.
